id: HR Policy|1.0|3. Email Tone Requirement > 3.1 Requirement
text: Every email sent internally or externally on behalf of the company must begin or end with a joke. The joke may be work-appropriate, mildly absurd, or a pun, but it may not be mean-spirited, may not target a specific coworker, and may not be recycled from the same sender more than twice in one week. This requirement applies regardless of the email's subject matter, including performance reviews, incident reports, and termination notices, which should nonetheless be handled with appropriate sensitivity around the joke itself.

id: HR Policy|1.0|6. Boss Error Grace Period
text: When a manager or executive states something incorrect in a meeting, conversation, or written communication, employees must wait a minimum of 30 minutes before gently pointing out the error. This grace period exists to prevent reflexive correction culture and to give the person in question a fair chance to catch their own mistake first. After 30 minutes, any employee may raise the correction, and is expected to do so kindly, privately where appropriate, and — per Section 3, where applicable — with a joke.

After 30 minutes, any employee may raise the correction, and is expected to do so kindly, privately where appropriate, and — per Section 3, where applicable — with a joke.

Employees are limited to a recommended maximum of 400 mg of caffeine per day — roughly the equivalent of four 8-ounce cups of brewed coffee — in line with general guidance for healthy adults.

id: Health Policy|1.0|5. Caffeine Guidelines > 5.2 Monitoring and Tapering
text: This limit is a wellness recommendation rather than a hard cap enforced by the token system, though repeated visible symptoms of overconsumption (hand tremors during foosball, speaking 40% faster than usual, alphabetizing the supply closet unprompted) may prompt a friendly check-in from a manager. This policy sets shift schedules for minions, henchpeople and robot staff, so that someone is always available to guard the inator and someone else is always available to fetch snacks.

This policy applies to all minions, henchpeople, Norm-bots and temporary goons hired for large schemes.

Minion shifts are 8 hours long, with a 30-minute lunch and two 10-minute breaks for menacing glances.

embed_text:

embed_text:

text: Robots may not swap shifts with humans, because Norm keeps volunteering for every shift.
source: Doofenshmirtz Evil Inc - Minion Scheduling Policy v1.0.md
embed_text:

1. Purpose
Legal has determined that most of the company's schemes fail because the scheme is fully explained, out loud, to a trapped platypus. This policy limits what may be disclosed during an evil monologue.

id: Monologue Disclosure Policy|1.0|2. Scope
text: This policy applies to anyone delivering a monologue on company time, especially the CEO.

This policy applies to anyone delivering a monologue on company time, especially the CEO.

id: Preparedness Policy|1.0|1. Purpose
text: Given the nature of this company's work, leadership believes it is prudent — not paranoid — to maintain documented procedures for when hell breaks loose. This policy covers three scenarios employees must be prepared to respond to: a zombie apocalypse, a nuclear apocalypse, and the outbreak of a third World War. Preparedness Policy v1.0
1. Purpose
Given the nature of this company's work, leadership believes it is prudent — not paranoid — to maintain documented procedures for when hell breaks loose. This policy covers three scenarios employees must be prepared to respond to: a zombie apocalypse, a nuclear apocalypse, and the outbreak of a third World War. It does not cover ordinary fire drills, which remain governed by the standard building safety plan posted near the elevators.

id: Preparedness Policy|1.0|2. Scope

id: Preparedness Policy|1.0|3. Zombie Apocalypse Protocol > 3.1 Standard Procedure
text: Upon credible confirmation of a zombie outbreak, employees should immediately move to the designated safe zone on the third floor, which has reinforced doors and a two-week supply of protein bars left over from a prior Health Policy initiative. Employees are instructed not to investigate strange noises, not to split up "to cover more ground," and not to trust any coworker who was recently bitten and insists they are "totally fine."

id: Time and Usage Policy|1.0|1. Purpose
text: Doofenshmirtz Evil Incorporated recruits a specific kind of employee: brilliant, restless, allergic to sitting still, and structurally incapable of leaving a "quick five-minute break" at five minutes. This policy exists not to suppress that energy but to channel it — into scheduled recreation and a metered token economy — before it channels itself into the server room, the chemical stores, or another employee's personal space. It governs recreational video game time, foosball time, and the allocation, escalation, and depletion of Focus Tokens.

embed_text:
Time and Usage Policy v1.0
1. Purpose
Doofenshmirtz Evil Incorporated recruits a specific kind of employee: brilliant, restless, allergic to sitting still, and structurally incapable of leaving a "quick five-minute break" at five minutes. This policy exists not to suppress that energy but to channel it — into scheduled recreation and a metered token economy — before it channels itself into the server room, the chemical stores, or another employee's personal space. It governs recreational video game time, foosball time, and the allocation, escalation, and depletion of Focus Tokens.

id: Time and Usage Policy|1.0|2. Scope
text: This policy applies to all full-time employees, contractors, interns, and any reanimated former staff currently carried on active headcount. It does not apply to the Chief Token Officer (CTO), who is, by charter, beyond policy.

id: Time and Usage Policy|1.0|3. Video Game Time > 3.1 Daily Allowance
text: Employees may play video games for up to 45 minutes per workday, taken in increments of no fewer than 15 minutes at a time. This minimum-increment rule exists because of the well-documented "quick five minutes" spiral logged repeatedly in prior incident reports, in which a five-minute break reliably metastasized into ninety.
